canonicalJson: UTF-8 without escapes, sorted keys, 2-space indent, LF, one trailing newline, numbers to at most three decimals
codes: Each invalid case records the validator's stable rule code; `rule` is the human name.
description: Fixtures for the rules a Plannotation 0.1 validator applies beyond the schema. Every document here -- valid and invalid alike -- is schema-valid against plannotation/schema/plannotation-0.1.json with zero errors: that is the point of the corpus, which describes documents that pass the schema and are still wrong. For the schema's own negative cases see tests/fixtures/plannotations/. Every file under valid/ is expected to produce no finding at all. Every file under invalid/ is expected to produce exactly one finding, of the stated severity, for the stated rule, at reportPath. reportPath is written in python-jsonschema json_path syntax and pointer is the same location as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, which is the form SPEC 4.4 (2) requires. The path names the smallest member whose value is wrong; where a rule constrains a relation among several members it names the smallest member that holds them all, and where the member that is wrong is one that is absent it names the object that should have carried it. For a uniqueness violation it names the later of the colliding occurrences, in the order viewports, elements, annotations. rule is a stable slug; several fixtures may share one, because one rule applied to two subjects is still one rule and must have one implementation. severity is error for a violation of a MUST and warning for a violation of a SHOULD or for a finding that rests on a tolerance or a heuristic, per SPEC 4.4. level is the conformance level SPEC 4.1 requires the validator to report, which it MUST do whether or not it also reports errors. documentPageCount, where present, is the page count of the document the label belongs to, which the target.pdfPage rule needs and a lone page label cannot carry. buildsThroughModel is false for the fixtures plannotation.model refuses at load time; those were written as JSON directly and a validator must reach their rule without going through the models.

invalid.description: The writer derived its annotation ids from the element table and emitted the window's id twice: the fire-rating tag is called e-win-14, which is already an element. Neither id is referenced from anywhere, so nothing else on the page becomes ambiguous -- only the uniqueness rule is broken. The path is the later of the two occurrences in the order viewports, elements, annotations.
invalid.note: plannotation.model refuses this document at load time, so a validator that reaches this rule only by calling load_plannotation will report one finding saying the schema accepts the document and the model does not, at the document root, rather than this rule at reportPath. reportPath records where the rule's own finding belongs; which of the two a run produces is a fact about the validator's architecture, and is worth asserting either way.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: every viewport, element and annotation id MUST be unique across all three collections, which share one namespace.

invalid.description: The window is placed in vp-sec-2, a second section viewport that was cut from the sheet without the elements being repointed. The label declares vp-sec, vp-key and vp-title and nothing else.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: element.viewport MUST reference a viewport in this label. A reference that does not resolve is an error.

invalid.description: The grid dimension names vp-section, a viewport id from the authoring tool's own vocabulary, where the sheet calls it vp-sec. The same rule as the case before it, applied to an annotation rather than an element.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: annotation.viewport MUST reference a viewport in this label.

invalid.description: The 12,000 dimension runs from the west wall to a column called e-col-99, which the page does not declare -- the column was renumbered and the dimension was not followed through. The dimension still draws the length it prints, so nothing but the reference is wrong.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: every measures entry MUST reference an element, or an annotation of type grid or level, in this label.

invalid.description: The dimension names a-tag-w1, which resolves -- it is a real id on the page -- but it is a tag. This is the case that distinguishes 'the reference resolves' from 'the reference resolves to something it may name'; a validator that only checked the id existed would pass it.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: measures admits an element, or an annotation of type grid or level, and nothing else. A tag is not a thing a dimension can run to.

invalid.description: The tag prints 'Pos. W1' and says it shows the Tag of e-wall-09. The wall on this page is e-wall-01; e-wall-09 is on no page at all.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: annotation.shows.element MUST reference an element in this label.

invalid.description: The tag says it prints the concrete cover out of Pset_ConcreteElementGeneral. The wall carries Pset_WallCommon and nothing else, so the absence is a positive fact about the element rather than a label that simply did not copy its property sets in. The printed text was changed with the reference so that the tag stays coherent; the rule it breaks is the reference, not the text.
invalid.violates: Design brief 8.2 requires that shows references resolve; shows.property names a property set and a property within it, and the element carries no such set.

invalid.description: The fire-rating tag keeps the property path and loses the element it was to be read from, as happens when the wall is re-exported under a new id and only half the reference is repaired. The shows object is still substantive, so the annotation still counts as linked and the sheet still reaches L3.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: shows.property names a property of the element shows.element identifies, so a property with no element to read it from resolves to nothing. Reported as a warning: 4.5 states no MUST for it, and a property named with no element is useless rather than misleading.

invalid.description: The section mark on the key plan points at vp-sec-b on sheet ARC-301, which is this sheet -- the section was split into A-A and B-B and the mark was left pointing at the id the split created. This is the third place a localId reference appears, after element.viewport and annotation.viewport, and the only one where a foreign id is sometimes legal: valid/01 carries a callout whose viewportId belongs to ARC-511, which must not be reported.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: target.viewportId is a localId interpreted in the targeted page. Where target.sheetId names this very sheet, the targeted page is this one and the reference MUST resolve on it like any other.

invalid.description: The callout points at PDF page 40 of a 14-page issue -- the index survived a set being split in two. This rule needs the document, not the label: documentPageCount records the page count the validator is to be given, and the clean control carries the same count with pdfPage 9.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.5: target.pdfPage is a zero-based page index within the same document and MUST be less than that document's page count.

invalid.description: The room dimension loses its measures and links to nothing. SPEC 4.1 is explicit that this is a quality signal and not a level boundary: the sheet still reaches L3 on its grid and its tag, because 'making it one would let a single unlinked dimension among fifty demote a sheet, which tells a consumer less, not more'. Every other fixture in this corpus keeps all five linkable types linked, so this is the only file that raises it.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.1: a writer SHOULD link every annotation of the types that usually can be linked -- dimension, tag, callout, sectionMark, grid -- that has a referent, and a validator SHOULD report any that are unlinked as a warning.

invalid.description: The revision cloud's box reaches y = 598 on a 594 mm sheet. It names no viewport, so nothing but the page rule applies to it, and the overshoot is 4 mm -- eight times the tolerance that valid/03 proves is real.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.4 (6) and design brief 8.3: every bbox lies inside the page, to within the geometric tolerance of 0.5 mm. The box stands 4 mm above a 594 mm page.

invalid.description: The column's box is written right edge first, x1 = 377 < x0 = 383. The box still covers the right ground and still lies on the page and inside its viewport, so the ordering rule is the only one it breaks -- which is exactly why the rule has to be checked separately.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.4: a bbox is [x0, y0, x1, y1] with x0 <= x1 and y0 <= y1. The ordering cannot be expressed in JSON Schema, so schema validity does not imply it; a validator MUST check it and MUST report it as an error.

invalid.description: Grid line B was lengthened at the top but its bounding box was not recomputed, so the line's upper end stands 2 mm above the box that is supposed to contain it. valid/04 is the same edit at 0.4 mm, which passes.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.4: where an object carries both a paperBBox and geometry, every point of that geometry MUST lie within the bounding box, to within 0.5 mm.

invalid.description: The plan viewport's frame reaches y = 600 on a 594 mm sheet. Everything drawn in it is still inside it, so no element or annotation is affected and the viewport's own box is the only thing wrong.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.4 (6) and design brief 8.3: viewport boxes do not exceed the page. This is the same rule as invalid/09, applied to a viewport; the design brief names the two cases separately and one implementation must serve both.

invalid.description: The north wall runs 12 mm past the right edge of the plan viewport: the wall is clipped by the viewport frame on the sheet but the writer emitted its untrimmed bounds. The box is still on the page. This is the corpus's proof that a validator separates warnings from errors -- a label with warnings and no errors is conforming.
invalid.violates: Design brief 8.3: elements' boxes inside their viewport's, as a warning and not an error. SPEC 4.4 gives this very case as its example of a warning, because it is legitimate for a tag drawn in the margin.

invalid.description: The plane's y axis is 1.002 long -- a direction taken from the model and never normalised. It is still orthogonal to the x axis and the view normal still comes out along +z, so the plane origin still agrees with the cut height and only the axis length is wrong.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.6: xAxis and yAxis MUST be unit vectors, to within 1e-6. Scale is already carried by paperToPlane, and an axis of another length would state it a second time.

invalid.description: The wing this plan covers is set out on a grid rotated about 16 degrees from model north. The writer turned the view's x axis to follow it and left the y axis on model north, so the pair describes a sheared plane that P = origin + X*xAxis + Y*yAxis does not mean. Both axes are still exactly unit length, so only orthogonality is broken; the path is the plane rather than either axis, because neither is wrong on its own.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.6: xAxis and yAxis MUST be mutually orthogonal, to within 1e-6. Their dot product here is 0.28.

invalid.description: The matrix was written row-major -- [a, b, c, d] laid out as the rows of the 2x2 rather than in the PDF order of SPEC 3.5 -- so b and c swapped and the determinant came out 0. Every paper point now maps to Y = -10. SPEC 3.5 forbids checking scale against a transform whose linear part is not a similarity, so the scale disagreement this creates is not a second finding.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.5: a writer MUST NOT emit a transform whose determinant is zero; such a transform collapses the viewport to a line and cannot be inverted. SPEC 4.4 (6) lists a singular paperToPlane among the geometric errors.

invalid.description: The transform was built from the SVG the drawing was cut from and the y-flip of SPEC 3.3 was never applied, so d is negative and the determinant is -0.0025. The magnitude still matches 1:50 exactly; only the handedness is wrong, which is the whole point -- a mirrored plan reads as its own reflection and nothing else in the label says so.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.5: a writer MUST NOT emit a transform whose determinant is negative, and a validator MUST report a negative determinant as an error. A mirror in the transform contradicts the orientation the plane's axes already state.

invalid.description: The viewport says 1:50 and its transform scales by 0.02 m per paper millimetre, which is 1:20 -- the view was rescaled and only the printed scale followed. The determinant is positive and the linear part is a similarity, so the transform is perfectly invertible; it simply contradicts the number beside it.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.5: where a viewport carries both scale and paperToPlane and the linear part is a similarity, the two MUST agree to within 0.1 %; a validator MUST report a disagreement. SPEC 4.4 (6) names a scale-contradicting paperToPlane among the geometric errors.

invalid.description: The storey's finished floor is at 3.5 m and the plan is cut 1.2 m above it, so the cutting plane is at 4.7 m; the origin says 3.5, the elevation written twice with the Schnitthoehe forgotten. SPEC 3.6 says a writer that cannot satisfy this 'has misplaced one of the three', so a validator cannot name which member is wrong: the path is the viewport, the smallest member holding all three.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.6: where both storey.elevation and cutHeight are present, the component of plane.origin along the plane normal MUST equal their sum. A validator MUST check this.

invalid.description: The room grew from 11.7 m to 12.5 m in the model and the dimension's value was edited on the sheet, but the drawing was never regenerated, so the line still runs 234 mm of paper. The gap is 800 mm, far outside any tolerance the rule could be given.
invalid.violates: The dimension's value must be the length it draws at its viewport's scale: 234 mm of paper at 1:50 is 11.7 m, and the label says 12.5 m. Reported as a warning: SPEC 4.4 (6) enumerates the geometric violations a validator MUST report and this is not among them, and SPEC 4.4 defines a warning as a finding that depends on a tolerance or a heuristic -- here, that the dimension line's path length is the quantity the value states, which a jogged or broken dimension legitimately breaks. The design brief puts re-measurement under the optional --ifc cross-check of 8.4, not under the errors of 8.3.

invalid.description: The model block survives with its filename and hash and loses its length unit, as happens when the unit is read from a different code path than the rest of the header. The transform is still invertible and right-handed, and its scale can no longer be checked against the viewport's at all -- SPEC 3.5 makes that comparison depend on the unit -- so this one omission costs the label the whole of what a transform is for. The path is the viewport rather than $.model because it is the viewport carrying paperToPlane that triggers the obligation, and a label may carry several of which only some do.
invalid.violates: SPEC 3.5: the output of paperToPlane is in the model's length unit, and a writer that emits paperToPlane MUST also emit model.lengthUnit. A reader that meets a transform without one MUST NOT assume a unit and MUST NOT report a distance derived from it as a length.

invalid.description: The column was recovered off the old formwork drawing rather than taken from the model, and says so honestly with a confidence of 0.78 -- but the label still calls itself authored. The item is right and the aggregate is wrong, so the finding belongs on the top-level member.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.6.4: the top-level provenance MUST be authored if and only if every value in the label is authored, and mixed otherwise. One element is inferred, so the aggregate is mixed.

invalid.description: The west wall says it was reconstructed and does not say how sure the reconstruction is. The schema cannot express the dependency, so the document is schema-valid. plannotation.model refuses it at load time, in Element's own validator, so a validator that reaches this rule only through the models will see an exception and not a finding: this rule has to be checked against the parsed JSON. The path is the object, because the member that is wrong is the one that is absent.
invalid.note: plannotation.model refuses this document at load time, so a validator that reaches this rule only by calling load_plannotation will report one finding saying the schema accepts the document and the model does not, at the document root, rather than this rule at reportPath. reportPath records where the rule's own finding belongs; which of the two a run produces is a fact about the validator's architecture, and is worth asserting either way.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.6.5: an element or annotation whose effective provenance is inferred MUST carry a confidence, and a validator MUST report a missing confidence on an inferred object as an error.

invalid.description: The same rule as the case before it, reached by inheritance rather than by declaration: the tag says nothing about its provenance and the label says inferred, so 4.6.3 makes the tag inferred and 4.6.5 then wants a confidence. This one does load through plannotation.model, whose item rule only fires on an explicit 'inferred' -- so it is the case that shows what a validator built on the models can and cannot see by itself.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.6.3 and 4.6.5: an item that omits provenance takes the label's own, so this tag's effective provenance is inferred and it MUST carry a confidence.

invalid.description: The traced existing wall keeps its confidence of 0.72 but loses its provenance. Under 4.6.3 it inherits inferred, so it still carries the confidence it needs and the aggregate is still mixed -- nothing else breaks. What is lost is that the writer told every reader the wall was reconstructed by silence rather than by saying so, which under a mixed top level is a claim it cannot make.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.6.4: where the top-level provenance is mixed, a writer MUST record provenance on every element and every annotation.

invalid.description: The slab is authored and carries a confidence of 0.9, which has no meaning there and invites a reader to discount a value that is not in doubt. SPEC 4.6.5 makes the asymmetry deliberate: a missing confidence on an inferred item is an error because it withholds what makes the value safe to use, and a spurious one on an authored item is untidiness, so rejecting a label over it 'would serve nobody'.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.6.5: an object whose effective provenance is authored SHOULD NOT carry a confidence, and a validator SHOULD report one as a warning. A SHOULD is a warning under SPEC 4.4.

invalid.description: The existing door's position was traced off the survey and its type came from the model, and the writer recorded that honestly as mixed instead of following 4.6.2 and calling the whole object inferred. It keeps its confidence, so nothing else is wrong: the aggregate is still mixed and the object still says how sure it is.
invalid.violates: SPEC 4.6.2: a writer SHOULD NOT put mixed on an element or an annotation, because nothing in the format could say which of its members came from which source. A SHOULD NOT is a warning under SPEC 4.4, and 4.6.2 is explicit that this is advice and not a prohibition -- a conforming reader MUST accept the value and treat the object as containing inferred content.

covers: shows.element with a Pset property the element carries
target naming another sheet, whose viewportId is a foreign localId
target naming a viewport on this sheet
target.pdfPage inside the document's page count
valid.description: Section A-A at 1:50 on A1. Every reference on the page resolves: two dimensions measure grids and levels, one measures two elements, one tag shows an element's Tag and another a property of a property set the element carries, a callout targets another sheet and a section mark targets a viewport on this one.

covers: paperToPlane determinant positive and matching scale
a dimension whose value is its drawn length at 1:50
valid.description: Storey plan at 1:50 on A1. Every box is ordered and on the page, every element sits inside its viewport, the plane axes are orthonormal, the transform is invertible, right-handed and scales at exactly 1:50, the plane origin is storey.elevation + cutHeight, and the dimension's value is the length it draws at the viewport's scale.

covers: a bbox 0.4 mm off the page, which passes
valid.description: The same plan, with the revision cloud's box reaching 0.4 mm past the top trim edge. This is the fixture that proves the 0.5 mm geometric tolerance is real: the box leaves the page and the document is still conforming.
valid.proves: page containment is checked to within 0.5 mm, so a box 0.4 mm past the edge is not a finding

covers: SPEC 3.4 geometry within its bbox, to within 0.5 mm
annotation geometry 0.4 mm outside its bbox, which passes
element outline 0.35 mm outside its bbox, which passes
valid.description: The same plan, with the grid line running 0.4 mm past the top of its own bounding box and the north wall's outline standing 0.35 mm proud of the element's box. Both are inside the 0.5 mm tolerance of SPEC 3.4 and neither is a finding.
valid.proves: the geometry-within-bbox rule is checked to within 0.5 mm, in both of the places SPEC 3.4 applies it

covers: a viewport bbox exactly equal to the page
an element bbox exactly equal to its viewport's
a degenerate bbox, permitted by SPEC 3.4
geometry lying exactly on its bbox boundary
valid.description: A0 site plan at 1:500 bled to the trim edge. The site viewport's box is exactly the page, the site element's box is exactly the viewport's, the coordinate-net grid line is a degenerate box with y0 = y1 running the full width of the sheet, and its geometry lies exactly on that box.
valid.proves: containment is inclusive: a box coincident with the page, or with its viewport, is inside it, and a degenerate box is legal

covers: provenance authored at the top level and on every item
valid.description: Formwork plan at 1:50 on A2, written straight from the model. The top level is authored, every element and annotation is authored, and none carries a confidence.

covers: provenance mixed at the top level
authored and inferred items side by side
every item marked, as a mixed label requires
valid.description: Survey plan at 1:100 on A2: two walls came from the model and two elements plus one dimension were measured off the existing building. The top level is mixed and every element and annotation records its own provenance, as SPEC 4.6.4 requires of a mixed label.

covers: provenance inferred at the top level and on every item
a viewport with a scale but no plane and no paperToPlane
valid.description: A legacy sheet reconstructed from the drawing alone: no model block, no transform, and every element and annotation inferred with a confidence. The top level is inferred, which is what SPEC 4.6.4 requires of a label recovered entirely from an unlabelled drawing.
Page, sheet and two viewports and nothing else: the drawing has been set out but nothing on it has been described. SPEC 4.1 puts this at L1.

covers: annotations of types that have nothing to link to
no annotation link, so no L3
valid.description: Reinforcement plan whose four elements are described but whose annotations are a north arrow, a scale bar, a hatch legend and a concrete note -- four types SPEC 4.1 lists as having nothing to link to. No annotation carries a link, so the label stops at L2.

covers: a north elevation whose plane xAxis is -x
a level annotation agreeing with its viewport's transform
valid.description: North elevation at 1:100 whose single linked annotation -- a tag showing a window's Tag -- is enough to reach L3. The plane's axes are xAxis -x and yAxis +z, so the normal points north and the view is seen from the north, per SPEC 3.6.
